text:
sam: seeing a lot of apiserver 503s in ap-southeast1 since ~06:20 UTC, looks correlated with etcd leader flips. Pod create ops for gpu-pool-asia are timing out.
liu: ta, I'm seeing raft leader changes in etcd metrics around the same time. leader_changes_total spiked to 9 in 5m.
marie: controller-manager logs show `WatchError: etcdserver: request timed out` repeated, and many `failed to create pod` errors for gpu provisioning.
devon: ops-bot reports increased network retransmits on the control-plane NICs in that region, egress NAT CPU also high. Could be noisy neighbor on host or MTU mismatch after the infra kernel update last night.
sam: rolling back that kernel on one controlplane node helped briefly (apiserver accepted requests) but leader flip resumed after ~3m.
liu: here are the relevant snippets from etcd logs:

```
2026-03-18T06:20:31Z etcd1 etcdserver: rejected proposal: no leader
2026-03-18T06:20:32Z etcd1 rafthttp: transport: write tcp 10.4.2.8:2380: write: connection reset by peer
2026-03-18T06:20:33Z etcd1 etcdserver: apply entries took too long [300ms for 1 entries]
```

marie: controller-manager stacktrace shows backlog in the workqueue. A bunch of GPU nodebinding controllers are retrying and consuming CPU.
devon: GPU onboarding jobs are timing out while waiting for node labels, so autoscaler keeps launching new instances and thrashing the quota tracker.
sre-oncall: adding context: the region has a low spare GPU capacity pool and we're on a burst quota. When many requests queue, we fallback to API polling which compounds apiserver load.
liu: hypothesis: transient network glitches between control plane members (pkt loss/retransmit) + kernel update changed NIC offload that increased latency, causing election timeouts. Etcd election timeout is 1s in this cluster, might be too aggressive for current noisy network.
sam: options:
- increase etcd election timeout (short term)
- pin leader to a stable node (ugly)
- roll back kernel across control plane (we tried on one node)
- throttle GPU scale-outs to reduce controller churn
- provision a small reserved Dedicated GPU pool for region-critical traffic (costy)

marie: immediate mitigations: switch autoscaler to conservative mode for ap-southeast1 (reduce burst), and set controller-manager QPS burst lower so repolling isn't hammering apiserver.
devon: I can set autoscaler to conservative now. Reducing scale-out frequency should cut the churn.
liu: I'll bump election timeout to 3s on the non-candidate nodes and monitor; will push in canary to one nodeset.
sre-oncall: please also enable more verbose raft logging for 15m window so we can confirm network vs leader behavior.
ops-bot: deploy request accepted by ci-cd for: `k8s-autoscaler:conservative-mode=true` by devon; rollout started to ap-southeast1.
sam: noted. are we comfortable with the customer impact of slowed GPU provisioning? Some fairness for long-running jobs might slip.
marie: short-term tradeoff better than flapping apiserver. We'll notify platform-users in #help with ETA on throughput hit.
devon: done — posted status in #help with a note: "GPU provisioning in ap-southeast1 may be slower while we stabilize control plane" :warning:
liu: canary bump applied to one control-plane node; raft logs show fewer timeouts so far. Will keep monitoring for 10m.
sre-oncall: please collect pod create latencies, apiserver 5xx rate, etcd leader_changes_total every 1m and share graph.
liu: attaching quick numbers (1m avg): etcd leader_changes_total +6, apiserver 5xx rate 0.18 -> 0.03, kube-controller-manager workqueue depth 120 -> 18.
sam: looks promising. Next steps: 1) keep autoscaler conservative for 2 hours, 2) if stable, roll election timeout change to remaining nodes, 3) evaluate whether network offload settings from kernel update should be reverted clusterwide, 4) ops to check host-level NIC telemetry for the noisy hosts.
marie: assign follow-ups: devon (autoscaler revert after window), liu (etcd/election rollout), sam (status note to infra-ops and cost team about possible reserved pool), sre-oncall (postmortem if flapping resumes).

sre-oncall: creating incident ticket INC-20260318-237 and linking logs.
marie: thanks — will update postmortem template with impact on GPU capacity and cost implications (reserved pool cost vs outage risk).
liu: current plan reduces immediate risk. if leader changes return after election timeout bump, we'll escalate to kernel revert across control plane.
sam: appreciated. ping me if we need to flip to reserve capacity; call page if apiserver 5xx > 0.2 sustained for 5m.

devon: one more note — autoscaler conservative mode buys us time but means some spot preemptible pools will be skipped, which will slightly increase spend on on-demand if we manually fill.
marie: add that to the incident ticket, we'll include a rough cost estimate.

sre-oncall: monitoring window active. keeping channel open for updates. :eyes:
